strategies.name: Baseline sequential all-reduce stages
strategies.desc: Performs 8 sequential all-reduce operations with interleaved local bidiagonal coupling and inverse coupling transformations, exactly as in the reference. 8 all-reduce dispatches, each operating on full W*S tensor. Straightforward but no overlap or fusion opportunities; maximizes simplicity at cost of latency.

strategies.name: Reduce-scatter then all-gather per stage
strategies.desc: Replace each all-reduce with a reduce-scatter followed by all-gather, allowing each rank to own and compute its shard's coupling locally before broadcasting. 16 collective dispatches (8 reduce-scatter + 8 all-gather). Trades dispatch count for smaller per-rank working set and potential pipeline benefits if hardware supports concurrent RS/AG.

strategies.name: Fused bidiagonal coupling with buffering
strategies.desc: Pre-compute all 8 stages' coupling and inverse-coupling coefficients, then issue all-reduces on pre-transformed buffers in a tight loop with minimal synchronization barriers. Still 8 all-reduce dispatches but local compute is batched/vectorized across stages. Reduces CPU overhead and enables better cache utilization for local ops.

strategies.name: Hierarchical two-level collective with nodes
strategies.desc: Exploit num_nodes structure by performing intra-node all-reduce first (ppn ranks), then inter-node all-reduce (node leaders), then intra-node broadcast, per stage. 24 dispatches (8 stages × 3 ops) but each operates on smaller subgroups. Benefits from faster intra-node interconnect; trades off dispatch count for reduced per-dispatch latency on large world size.

strategies.name: Pipelined ring-allreduce with coupling overlap
strategies.desc:
Implement custom ring-based all-reduce using send/recv primitives where each rank pipelines the coupling transformation during the reduce-scatter phase and inverse during all-gather phase. Approximately 2*W*8 send/recv dispatches but enables computation-communication overlap. High dispatch count but hides local arithmetic latency within network transfers.
